items.title: Hadjar cleared to return for Red Bull at the Azerbaijan GP; Lawson back to Racing Bulls
items.summary: Isack Hadjar has been declared fit to return to the Red Bull cockpit at Baku after recovering from the fractured wrist he suffered training over the summer break, which had kept him out of Zandvoort, Monza and Madrid. Liam Lawson, who deputised at Red Bull for those three races, returns to Racing Bulls, and Yuki Tsunoda reverts to his reserve-driver role after covering Lawson's seat.
items.why_it_matters: This replaces the prior 'Hadjar still sidelined' storyline outright: Red Bull's regular line-up (Verstappen/Hadjar) and Racing Bulls' regular line-up are both back for this round, not the replacement chain used across the last three races.

items.title: Ferrari weighing a Baku grid penalty for Leclerc as fifth power unit looms
items.summary: The Race reports Ferrari's development has stalled since its Barcelona win, with the SF-26's Zandvoort floor update only around three-quarters of the package originally planned; the rest is now targeted for Austin. Separately, following extensive checks after Leclerc's Monza accident, Ferrari raced Madrid on his older ADUO 1 power unit, and both Hamilton and Leclerc are certain to take a new unit before the season ends. The Race reports Ferrari is considering unlocking Leclerc's fifth unit (in ADUO 2 specification) as early as this Baku weekend, which would trigger a grid penalty at a circuit where overtaking is considered achievable; the team says the final call will be made during the weekend after running the Monza-spec unit in practice.
items.why_it_matters: This is a specific, dated (20 September) technical/penalty story tied directly to this round, not a season generality: a grid-penalty decision for Leclerc could be confirmed during the Baku weekend itself. Keep it framed as reported rumour/likely scenario pending Ferrari's actual declaration, and distinguish it from Hamilton's separate, later-race unit decision.

sources.label: The Race: Why Ferrari's F1 progress stalled - and what it plans to do

items.title: Williams brings its long-awaited FW48 upgrade package to Baku
items.summary: Williams will introduce a major, long-delayed upgrade package for the FW48 at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix after failing to score a point since Monaco. Drivers Alex Albon and Carlos Sainz say the package should bring a genuine step but caution it is unlikely to be the full gain calculated when it was signed off months ago, since rival midfield teams have kept developing in the meantime; team principal James Vowles calls the round a proof point for the team's processes ahead of the 2027 car (FW50).
items.why_it_matters: This is a concrete, sourced upgrade claim tied specifically to this round, not a season-long generality — note it is expected to close the gap rather than move Williams into Q3 contention, and that both drivers have already tempered expectations publicly before the sessions.

sources.label: Formula1.com: Why the FW48 upgrade package in Baku is so crucial for Williams

items.title: F1's data team maps the earliest Antonelli could clinch the 2026 title
items.summary: Formula1.com's data team calculated the title-clinch scenarios after Antonelli's Spanish GP win: he leads Russell by 81 points and Hamilton by 101 with nine rounds (233 points maximum, including the Singapore Sprint) remaining. If Antonelli fails to score again, Russell could clinch as early as São Paulo, Hamilton/Norris/Leclerc at Las Vegas, Verstappen/Piastri not before Qatar. If Antonelli wins Azerbaijan, Bahrain and both Singapore sessions while Russell scores nothing, he could clinch at Singapore (Round 17). Using each driver's actual season median finish instead, the earliest projected clinch is Round 19 in Mexico.
items.why_it_matters: This supersedes the earlier Russell/Hamilton 'concede the title' framing with the publication's own concrete point gaps and clinch-date scenarios, tied to the current standings after Spain rather than a general concession quote.

sources.label: Formula1.com: POINTS PERMUTATIONS — When is the earliest Antonelli could win the World Championship?

items.title: Piastri looks to bounce back from an 'anonymous' Madrid weekend
items.summary: Oscar Piastri says he needs to 'figure out how to close that gap' after what he described as an anonymous weekend in Madrid, as team-mate Lando Norris and championship leader Kimi Antonelli have pulled further ahead in recent rounds.
items.why_it_matters: A direct, dated driver quote framing Piastri's own title outlook heading into Baku, distinct from the separate Russell/Hamilton concession story above and from McLaren's constructors' position.
